dedupe_keys.name: gtap standard computable general equilibrium model

description: The standard GTAP model is a multiregion, multisector computable general equilibrium model with perfect competition and constant returns to scale. Its features include non-homothetic CDE household preferences, explicit international trade and transport margins, Armington bilateral trade and a global banking sector linking savings and investment, with closure options for unemployment, tax revenue replacement, fixed trade balances and partial equilibrium comparisons. It is maintained by the Center for Global Trade Analysis at Purdue University; version 7 was documented by Corong and colleagues in the Journal of Global Economic Analysis in 2017, and five major versions have been released since 1994, alongside a dynamic model and others. Coverage is global, at the regional and sectoral detail of the GTAP data base. The documentation is public and the model is run through RunGTAP; the data base is priced, with archived releases free. Caveats: the standard model is comparative static, and results depend on the aggregation and elasticities chosen, and the page read does not state licence terms. For simulation it estimates how trade shocks, export bans or the loss of a production region spread through global supply chains and prices, supporting resilience studies of industrial and food systems. It is related to the GTAP Data Base and GEMPACK records in this catalogue.
